name: Sika® Block
summary: Sika® Block is a biodegradable synthetic based admixture for masonry block manufacture. Sika® Block is designed for use with zero or low slump concrete commonly used in the manufacture of masonry blocks.
metaDescription: Sika® Block is a biodegradable synthetic based admixture for masonry block manufacture. Sika® Block is designed for use with zero or low slump concrete commonly used in the manufacture of masonry blocks.
attributes: Improved Workability and Finishing as well as Appearance
Reduces Tear and Wear on Machinery
By increasing the production rates, cost reduction will be achieved
Maintaining the long term appearance as well as strength
usage: Sika® Block is utilised where an improvement in appearance of the masonry unit is required. This is achieved by creating better slick, improving moldability, enhancing cohesion and increasing early age strength. Sika® Block performs best when added to low slump masonry block mixes. It provides a more efficient utilisation of mixing water by aiding the dispersion of cement particles. Sika® Block will also improve the appearance and density of masonry units.
advantages: Improved Workability and Finishing as well as Appearance
Reduces Tear and Wear on Machinery
By increasing the production rates, cost reduction will be achieved
Maintaining the long term appearance as well as strength
packaging: Bulk deliveries 1000 litre IBC 205 litre drum 10 litre container

items.label: Shelf life
items.text: Stored at temperatures between 5°C and 35°C in unopened original containers protected from direct sunlight and frost, shelf life is one (1) year.

items.label: Storage conditions
items.text: Store at temperature between 5° and 35°, protected from direct sunlight.

items.label: Dispensing
items.text: Sika® Block should be added with mixing water to ensure correct dispersion and maximum performance.

items.label: Recommended dosage
items.text: Sika® Block can be used at rates of 150-500mls per 100kg of total cementitious material. Optimum dosage should be determined by site trials.
